intro: Window repair is the adjustment or replacement of a specific failed part of a window, such as a snapped sash cord, a paint seal, or a worn hinge, carried out without replacing the window itself. FixWell Services repairs sash and casement windows across Salisbury and Wiltshire, with most call-outs involving the original timber sash windows found on the city's Victorian and Georgian terraces. Call +44 7391 599 078 or use the quote form for a free assessment.

sections.heading: What Window Repair Work FixWell Carries Out in Salisbury
sections.body: A window repair addresses one specific fault rather than replacing the frame or sash. FixWell re-cords sash windows whose cast-iron weights have dropped after the cord holding them has snapped, which is what causes a sash to fall shut on its own or refuse to stay open. Sashes painted shut over decades of redecoration are freed by carefully scoring along the paint seal without damaging the frame or glazing. Draught-proofing, in the form of a brush or compression strip fitted into the sash channel, is added where cold air is getting through. On casement windows, a binding or stiff hinge is eased and adjusted, and loose or cracked putty holding a pane in place is replaced.

sections.heading: Why Sash Windows Fail on Salisbury's Period Properties
sections.body: Sash cords made from braided cotton or nylon have a working life of roughly 15–25 years under constant friction against the pulley, and once one snaps, the cast-iron weight behind it drops inside the box frame with nothing left to counterbalance the sash. Multiple coats of gloss paint applied over generations of redecoration frequently seal the moving sash to the frame, which is why a window that 'won't open' is more often paint-bound than mechanically stuck. A worn parting bead lets the window rattle in strong wind, a fault Salisbury's exposed Wiltshire weather makes more noticeable than it would be in a sheltered location.

sections.heading: Casement Window Repairs
sections.body: A stiff or binding casement hinge is usually caused by a swollen frame or a loose screw fixing rather than a fault with the hinge itself, and re-tightening or replacing the screw resolves most cases without needing a new hinge. Cracked putty around a single pane is re-bedded with fresh glazing putty, matched to the existing profile so the repair doesn't stand out against the rest of the frame.

sections.heading: How FixWell Repairs a Sash or Casement Window
sections.body: Every window repair begins with identifying which of the four common faults is present: a snapped cord, a paint seal, a draught, or a binding hinge, since each needs a different fix. A snapped sash cord is replaced with new cord rated to the weight of the sash, and the sash is re-hung and tested through a full open-close cycle before the job is signed off. A painted-shut sash is scored along the seam with a specialist tool that separates the paint film without marking the timber underneath.

sections.heading: Cost and Timeframe for Window Repairs in Salisbury
sections.body: Re-cording a single sash typically costs £80–£180 per window, completed in one visit. Draught-proofing a full sash window costs £60–£120. Freeing a painted-shut sash runs £40–£90, and a casement hinge adjustment is usually £30–£70. These figures fall within FixWell's standard £20–£40 per hour rate, and a fixed-price quote is given once the specific fault has been identified.

sections.heading: Should You Repair or Replace an Original Sash Window?
sections.body: A well-maintained original sash window is usually repairable and, on a period Salisbury property, is worth preserving rather than replacing. The timber, once sound, will outlast most modern double-glazed replacements and keeps the property's original character intact. Severe rot in the box frame, a cracked sill, or structural movement in the surrounding masonry need a specialist joiner rather than a repair visit. FixWell's carpentry service covers this assessment as part of every window repair quote.

sections.heading: Draught-Proofing and Winter Energy Loss
sections.body: An unsealed gap around a sash window loses heat at a rate noticeable enough to affect a room's comfort within minutes of the heating switching off, which is why draught-proofing is one of the most cost-effective repairs relative to its impact. Fitting a brush or compression strip into the sash channel closes that gap without altering how the window operates. This is one item on FixWell's broader guide to preparing a home for winter.

sections.heading: Sash Windows and Salisbury's Period Property Character
sections.body: Original sash windows are a defining feature of Salisbury's Victorian and Georgian housing stock, and much of the city centre sits within a designated Conservation Area where replacing an original window with a modern unit can require planning consent. FixWell repairs original features, including sash windows, timber skirting, and period doors, rather than defaulting to replacement. Anyone planning a wider renovation should read FixWell's home renovation planning guide before committing to a scope.

faqs.q: Can you fix a sash window that won't stay open?
faqs.a: Yes. A sash that won't stay open or falls shut on its own almost always means the cord has snapped and the counterweight has dropped inside the frame. Re-cording replaces the cord and re-hangs the sash against its weight, restoring normal operation in one visit.

faqs.q: How do you free a window that's been painted shut?
faqs.a: The paint seal is carefully scored along the join between sash and frame with a specialist tool, separating the layers of paint without cutting into the timber underneath. Multiple coats built up over years of redecoration are the usual cause, not a mechanical fault.

faqs.q: Is it worth repairing an old sash window instead of replacing it?
faqs.a: In most cases, yes. Sound original timber outlasts many modern replacements once repaired, and Salisbury's Conservation Area rules can also restrict swapping original windows for modern units, so repair is often the more practical route.

faqs.q: Do you fit draught-proofing to sash windows in Salisbury?
faqs.a: Yes, typically £60–£120 for a full window using a brush or compression strip fitted into the sash channel, closing the gap that causes cold draughts without changing how the window opens.

Minor adjustment, such as a stiff hinge or handle, falls within scope. Sealed-unit replacement or mechanism failure on uPVC windows is typically a job for a specialist window company, and FixWell will say so clearly if that's what's needed.
